# BR-500 Control Narrative: Section X, pH and Dissolved Oxygen Control

**Document status:** DRAFT for review. Process Engineering, Automation, QA and Validation must approve it.
**System:** Emerson DeltaV DCS / DeltaV Batch (ISA-88)
**Unit:** BR-500, 2000 L single-use CHO bioreactor

> **Reader's note:** Each requirement has a unique ID (e.g. `PH-07`) so OQ test cases can trace to it. Values marked **[A]** are assumptions I introduced because the source information did not specify them. Each one is listed in Section X.10 and must be confirmed or corrected before approval. Tag names marked **[P]** are proposed, not confirmed.

---

## X.1 Scope

This section defines automatic control of culture pH and dissolved oxygen (DO) in BR-500, including:
- measurement selection,
- control strategy,
- base addition limit,
- phase-dependent behavior,
- alarms,
- audit requirements.

It excludes temperature, pressure, level, feed and antifoam control, and the internal logic of the Media Fill and Harvest phases, except where those phases interact with pH or DO control.

## X.2 Equipment and Tag List

| Tag | Description | Range / Units |
|---|---|---|
| AT-501A / AT-501B | pH transmitters, probes A and B | 0–14 pH (process range see PH-03) |
| AT-502A / AT-502B | DO transmitters, probes A and B | 0–200 % air saturation **[A]** |
| AY-501 **[P]** | pH measurement selection/averaging block | pH |
| AY-502 **[P]** | DO measurement selection/averaging block | % air sat |
| AIC-501 **[P]** | pH controller | 0–100 % output |
| AIC-502 **[P]** | DO controller (cascade primary) | 0–100 % output |
| FCV-510 / FIC-510 | CO₂ sparge mass flow controller | 0–2.0 slpm |
| P-520 / SC-520 **[P]** | 1 M Na₂CO₃ base addition pump | 0–100 % speed |
| WT-521 | Base bag load cell | kg |
| WQI-521 **[P]** | Cumulative base addition totalizer | L |
| SIC-530 | Agitator speed controller | 80–140 rpm (DO control range) |
| FCV-511 / FIC-511 | Air sparge mass flow controller | 0–10.0 slpm |
| FCV-512 / FIC-512 | O₂ sparge mass flow controller | 0–5.0 slpm |

## X.3 Phase Applicability

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| PD-01 | pH control (AIC-501) and DO control (AIC-502) shall be active only during the **Equilibrate**, **Inoculate** and **Production** phases. |
| PD-02 | During **Media Fill**, AIC-501 and AIC-502 shall be in MAN. The CO₂ sparge (FCV-510) shall be at 0 slpm, the base pump (P-520) stopped, and the O₂ sparge (FCV-512) at 0 slpm. Air sparge and agitator are under Media Fill phase control and outside this section. |
| PD-03 | On start of **Equilibrate**, the phase shall download the recipe setpoints (pH SP, DO SP) and place AIC-501 and AIC-502 in AUTO. SIC-530, FIC-510, FIC-511, FIC-512 and SC-520 shall be in CAS. |
| PD-04 | Control shall continue without bump across the Equilibrate → Inoculate → Production transitions. Phase transitions shall not re-initialize controller outputs or reset the base totalizer. |
| PD-05 | On start of **Harvest**, AIC-501 and AIC-502 shall be placed in MAN. FCV-510 shall go to 0 slpm, P-520 shall stop, and FCV-512 shall go to 0 slpm. SIC-530 and FIC-511 are released to Harvest phase control. |
| PD-06 | Outside Equilibrate–Production, the operator shall not be able to place AIC-501 or AIC-502 in AUTO. The DeltaV phase logic shall enforce this, and the faceplate shall indicate it. |
| PD-07 | **Phase HELD:** pH and DO control shall continue in AUTO at the current setpoints. The base limit interlock (Section X.6) remains active. **[A]** |
| PD-08 | **Phase STOPPED / ABORTED:** the actions of PD-05 shall be executed. **[A]** |

## X.4 Measurement Selection and Probe Health

### X.4.1 Probe health definition

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| MS-01 | A probe is **healthy** when all of the following are true: (a) the transmitter status is GOOD (not BAD/UNCERTAIN); (b) the PV is within the validity range (pH 5.50–8.50 **[A]**, DO 0–150 % **[A]**); (c) the probe has not been manually deselected by the operator. |
| MS-02 | A probe that becomes unhealthy shall be excluded from control within one controller scan. An alarm shall be raised identifying the probe and the reason. |
| MS-03 | A probe returning to healthy shall **not** be automatically re-included. It shall be re-included only after operator acknowledgement and re-selection, and the action shall be recorded in the audit trail. **[A]** |

### X.4.2 pH selection (AY-501)

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| PH-01 | When AT-501A and AT-501B are both healthy, the control PV shall be the arithmetic mean of the two. |
| PH-02 | When only one pH probe is healthy, the control PV shall be that probe's value, and a "pH single-probe control" alarm shall be active. |
| PH-03 | When neither probe is healthy, AIC-501 shall shed to MAN and P-520 shall stop. FCV-510 shall hold its last output **[A]**. A "pH control lost" alarm shall be raised (Critical priority). |
| PH-04 | When both probes are healthy and \|AT-501A − AT-501B\| > 0.10 pH **[A]** for 60 s **[A]**, a "pH probe deviation" alarm shall be raised. Control shall continue on the average. The operator may deselect one probe (MS-01c), entering a reason comment. |

### X.4.3 DO selection (AY-502)

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| DO-01 | When AT-502A and AT-502B are both healthy, the control PV shall be the arithmetic mean of the two. **[A]** (Source data did not specify DO averaging. See open item OI-1.) |
| DO-02 | When only one DO probe is healthy, the control PV shall be that probe's value, and a "DO single-probe control" alarm shall be active. |
| DO-03 | When neither probe is healthy, AIC-502 shall shed to MAN and hold all cascade outputs (agitator, air, O₂) at their last values **[A]**. A "DO control lost" alarm shall be raised (Critical priority). |
| DO-04 | When both probes are healthy and \|AT-502A − AT-502B\| > 10 % air sat **[A]** for 60 s **[A]**, a "DO probe deviation" alarm shall be raised. Control shall continue on the average. Operator deselection is per PH-04. |

## X.5 pH Control (AIC-501)

### X.5.1 Strategy

AIC-501 is a single PID controller. Its output is split-range between the acid side (CO₂ sparge) and the base side (base pump). The two sides shall never act at the same time.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| PH-10 | The default setpoint shall be pH 7.00, downloaded from the recipe. |
| PH-11 | The deadband shall be ±0.05 pH around SP, i.e. 6.95–7.05 at SP 7.00. **[A]** (Interpreted as half-width. See OI-2.) |
| PH-12 | **Acid side:** when PV > SP + 0.05, AIC-501 shall increase CO₂ sparge flow (FCV-510, 0–2.0 slpm) to lower pH. |
| PH-13 | **Base side:** base addition shall be permitted only when PV < SP − 0.05. P-520 shall stop when PV ≥ SP − 0.05. |
| PH-14 | **Within deadband** (SP − 0.05 ≤ PV ≤ SP + 0.05), the base pump shall be stopped. The CO₂ sparge shall hold its last output (no PID corrective action). **[A]** |
| PH-15 | **Split range:** AIC-501 output 0–45 % shall drive P-520 from 100 % to 0 %. Output 45–55 % shall be neutral, with no acid and no base. Output 55–100 % shall drive FCV-510 from 0 to 2.0 slpm. **[A]** |
| PH-16 | P-520 shall not run while FIC-510 flow is > 0.05 slpm **[A]**, and FCV-510 shall not be commanded open while P-520 is running. This mutual exclusion shall be implemented independently of the split-range calculation. |
| PH-17 | The CO₂ output shall be clamped to 0–2.0 slpm. Requests outside that range shall be limited, and the controller shall not wind up (DeltaV BKCAL/external reset). |
| PH-18 | Allowable pH setpoint entry range: 6.80–7.20 **[A]**. The system shall reject entries outside this range. |

### X.5.2 Base addition limit (WQI-521)

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| BL-01 | Cumulative base volume shall be calculated from WT-521 as: V = (W_ref − W_current) / ρ, with ρ = 1.10 kg/L **[A]** (to be confirmed by measurement of the 1 M Na₂CO₃ lot). Bag changes (BL-06) shall be accumulated into the total. |
| BL-02 | The totalizer shall reset to 0 L only at the start of Media Fill for a new batch. No other phase, operator or engineer action during a batch shall reset it. |
| BL-03 | At ≥ 36.0 L (90 % of limit) **[A]**, a "Base addition high" alarm shall be raised (High priority). |
| BL-04 | At ≥ 40.0 L, P-520 shall be stopped and base addition shall be inhibited for the remainder of the batch. A "Base limit reached" alarm shall be raised (Critical priority). The acid side of AIC-501 shall continue to operate. |
| BL-05 | The BL-04 interlock shall not be bypassable from the operator interface, or by operator or supervisor role, during a batch. Any continuation of base addition requires an engineering action under the site deviation process. That action is outside normal operation. |
| BL-06 | A "Base bag change" operator command shall freeze the totalizer and inhibit P-520. After the new bag is installed and the operator confirms, the totalizer shall capture a new W_ref and resume accumulation from the frozen value. The command shall be recorded in the audit trail. |
| BL-07 | If WT-521 goes BAD or out of range, P-520 shall stop and base addition shall be inhibited until WT-521 returns to GOOD. A "Base load cell fault" alarm shall be raised. (Fail-safe: the limit cannot be verified without the load cell.) |
| BL-08 | An unexpected increase of WT-521 > 0.5 kg **[A]** outside a bag-change sequence shall raise an alarm. The totalizer shall not decrease. |
| BL-09 | The current WQI-521 value shall be displayed on the BR-500 overview and recorded in the batch record at the end of Production. |

## X.6 DO Control (AIC-502)

### X.6.1 Strategy

AIC-502 is a single PID controller acting as the cascade primary. Its output is sequenced across three secondary loops in fixed order: agitation, then air, then O₂.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| DO-10 | The default setpoint shall be 40 % air saturation, downloaded from the recipe. |
| DO-11 | Split-range sequence: |

| AIC-502 output | SIC-530 agitator | FIC-511 air | FIC-512 O₂ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 – 33.3 % | 80 → 140 rpm | 0 slpm | 0 slpm |
| 33.3 – 66.7 % | 140 rpm (held at max) | 0 → 10.0 slpm | 0 slpm |
| 66.7 – 100 % | 140 rpm (held at max) | 10.0 slpm (held at max) | 0 → 5.0 slpm |

**[A]** These breakpoints use equal thirds. They are subject to tuning (OI-5).

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| DO-12 | While DO control is active, agitator speed shall not drop below 80 rpm, even at 0 % controller output. |
| DO-13 | A downstream stage shall not begin to increase until the upstream stage is at its maximum. On decreasing demand, stages shall unload in reverse order: O₂ first, then air, then agitation. |
| DO-14 | If a secondary loop is not in CAS (e.g. operator places FIC-511 in MAN), AIC-502 shall not wind up. The DO controller shall continue to act on the remaining available stages, and a "DO cascade broken" alarm shall be raised. **[A]** |
| DO-15 | Allowable DO setpoint entry range: 20–60 % air sat **[A]**. The system shall reject entries outside this range. |

## X.7 Alarms

All limits marked [A] require confirmation.

| ID | Alarm | Condition | Priority | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AL-01 | pH high | PV > SP + 0.20 for 5 min **[A]** | High | Alarm only |
| AL-02 | pH low | PV < SP − 0.20 for 5 min **[A]** | High | Alarm only |
| AL-03 | pH probe A/B fault | MS-01 fail | High | Per PH-02 |
| AL-04 | pH probe deviation | PH-04 | Medium | Alarm only |
| AL-05 | pH control lost | PH-03 | Critical | Per PH-03 |
| AL-06 | DO low | PV < SP − 10 % for 5 min **[A]** | High | Alarm only |
| AL-07 | DO high | PV > SP + 20 % for 5 min **[A]** | Medium | Alarm only |
| AL-08 | DO probe A/B fault | MS-01 fail | High | Per DO-02 |
| AL-09 | DO probe deviation | DO-04 | Medium | Alarm only |
| AL-10 | DO control lost | DO-03 | Critical | Per DO-03 |
| AL-11 | DO cascade at max | AIC-502 OUT ≥ 99 % for 10 min **[A]** | High | Alarm only |
| AL-12 | DO cascade broken | DO-14 | High | Per DO-14 |
| AL-13 | Base addition high | BL-03 | High | Alarm only |
| AL-14 | Base limit reached | BL-04 | Critical | Per BL-04 |
| AL-15 | Base load cell fault | BL-07 | High | Per BL-07 |

The pH and DO process alarms (AL-01, AL-02, AL-06, AL-07, AL-11) shall be suppressed outside Equilibrate–Production. Equipment fault alarms shall remain active.

## X.8 Setpoint Change Control and Audit Trail

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| AU-01 | During **Production**, any change to the pH SP or DO SP shall require the operator to enter a reason before the change is accepted. Supported mechanisms are a mandatory comment field or a selection from a predefined reason list plus free text. |
| AU-02 | If the reason is cancelled or left blank, the setpoint shall not change. |
| AU-03 | Each Production setpoint change shall be recorded in the batch record / DeltaV Event Chronicle with: the date/time, user ID, tag, old value, new value, reason, and batch ID. |
| AU-04 | During Production, setpoint changes shall be possible only through the controlled entry path that enforces AU-01: the recipe parameter / phase operator prompt. Direct SP writes from the AIC-501/AIC-502 faceplate shall be blocked. **[A]** (This prevents a faceplate write from bypassing the reason prompt.) |
| AU-05 | Setpoint changes shall be restricted to users with the Operator role or higher. Changes to deadband, split-range breakpoints, tuning, alarm limits and the base limit shall be restricted to the Engineer role and shall not be possible while a batch is active. **[A]** |
| AU-06 | During Production, the following shall also be recorded with user ID and timestamp: controller mode changes (AUTO/MAN/CAS), manual output changes, probe deselection/re-selection, and base bag changes. **[A]** (This exceeds the stated QA requirement. Recommended; see OI-7.) |
| AU-07 | Audit records shall be secure, time-stamped and non-editable, in accordance with 21 CFR Part 11 / EU GMP Annex 11. |

## X.9 OQ Test Derivation Guide

The table below suggests minimum OQ coverage. Each test should simulate the relevant inputs at the I/O or function-block level and verify the stated response.

| Test | Covers | Method / acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|
| OQ-01 | PD-01–PD-06 | Step the batch through every phase. Verify loop modes and output states at each transition, and that AUTO is refused outside Equilibrate–Production. |
| OQ-02 | PD-07, PD-08 | HOLD, STOP and ABORT in Production. Verify loops continue (HOLD) or go to the PD-05 states (STOP/ABORT). |
| OQ-03 | PH-01, DO-01 | Simulate A = 7.00 and B = 7.10. Verify PV = 7.05. Repeat for DO. |
| OQ-04 | MS-01, MS-02, PH-02, DO-02 | For each probe in turn, force BAD status and then out-of-range values. Verify exclusion within one scan and the alarm. |
| OQ-05 | MS-03 | Restore the faulted probe. Verify it is not re-included until operator re-selection, and that the action is audit-trailed. |
| OQ-06 | PH-03, DO-03 | Fail both probes. Verify shed to MAN and the specified output states. |
| OQ-07 | PH-04, DO-04 | Apply a deviation just below and just above the threshold, for less than and more than the delay. Verify alarm behavior. |
| OQ-08 | PH-11–PH-14 | Test PV at 6.94, 6.95, 7.00, 7.05 and 7.06. Verify base, acid and no action as specified, including exact boundary behavior. |
| OQ-09 | PH-15, PH-16 | Drive AIC-501 in MAN across 0–100 %. Verify the split-range mapping and neutral band. Force both actuators simultaneously and verify the interlock prevents it. |
| OQ-10 | PH-17, DO-14 | Saturate the outputs. Verify clamping and no windup on recovery. |
| OQ-11 | PH-18, DO-15 | Enter setpoints at, just inside and just outside the limits. Verify acceptance or rejection. |
| OQ-12 | BL-01 | Simulate a WT-521 decrease. Verify the calculated volume against ρ. |
| OQ-13 | BL-03, BL-04, BL-05 | Simulate 35.9, 36.0, 39.9 and 40.0 L. Verify the alarms, pump stop and acid side still active. Attempt a bypass and reset from operator and supervisor accounts and verify both are refused. |
| OQ-14 | BL-02 | Attempt a totalizer reset mid-batch and across phase transitions. Verify it is not possible. Verify reset at Media Fill of a new batch. |
| OQ-15 | BL-06, BL-08 | Execute a bag change. Verify freeze, re-reference and accumulation continuity. Simulate a weight increase without a bag change and verify the alarm. |
| OQ-16 | BL-07 | Fail WT-521 with base demand present. Verify the pump stops and stays stopped. |
| OQ-17 | DO-11–DO-13 | Ramp AIC-502 output 0 → 100 → 0 %. Verify stage order, holds at max, the 80 rpm minimum and reverse unloading. |
| OQ-18 | DO-14 | Place each secondary loop in MAN with DO control active. Verify the alarm and the behavior. |
| OQ-19 | AL-01–AL-15 | Trigger each alarm. Verify limit, delay, priority and phase-based suppression. |
| OQ-20 | AU-01–AU-03 | Change the pH and DO SP in Production with a reason, then with a blank or cancelled reason. Verify the audit record contents and that a blank or cancelled reason produces no change. |
| OQ-21 | AU-04, AU-05 | Attempt a faceplate SP write in Production, and engineering parameter changes with an active batch, under each user role. Verify both are refused. |
| OQ-22 | AU-06, AU-07 | Verify the recording of mode, output, probe and bag-change actions. Attempt to edit audit records and verify this is not possible. |

## X.10 Assumptions and Open Items (must be closed before approval)

| ID | Item |
|---|---|
| OI-1 | DO measurement selection: the source data specified averaging for pH only. Confirm whether DO should use the average, the lower of the two, or operator selection. |
| OI-2 | Deadband interpretation: confirm whether 0.05 is ±0.05 (band 6.95–7.05) or a total band width (±0.025). |
| OI-3 | In-deadband behavior: confirm that CO₂ holds its last value (PH-14), or whether it should ramp to 0 or a minimum flow. |
| OI-4 | Na₂CO₃ density (1.10 kg/L assumed), the 90 % pre-alarm level, and whether the 40 L limit is an absolute hard stop (BL-05). |
| OI-5 | DO split-range breakpoints, any minimum air sparge or overlay flow, total gas flow limits, and whether CO₂ sparge must be considered in total sparge rate. |
| OI-6 | Probe validity ranges, deviation limits and delays, process alarm limits, and SP entry ranges. Process Development should provide these. |
| OI-7 | QA to confirm whether the AU-06 extended audit scope and AU-04 faceplate lockout are required, and whether a second-person verification (witness signature) is needed for Production setpoint changes. |
| OI-8 | Behavior of loops on phase HOLD/STOP/ABORT (PD-07, PD-08), and on DCS controller switchover or power loss. |
| OI-9 | Controller tag names marked [P]. Align these with the P&ID and the DeltaV configuration standard. |
| OI-10 | Whether pH/DO setpoint changes during Equilibrate and Inoculate also require a reason. The source requirement covers Production only. |
